rooms.name: Clay Gate
rooms.description: Wet fingerprints from three generations remain in the half-fired gateposts.

encounters.cue: Compare the prints on the gatepost.
encounters.result: The smallest thumb fits inside a larger print. Both have the same crescent scar, one on the left hand and one on the right.

rooms.name: Test Tile Rack
rooms.description: Tiny fired tiles record what the kiln looked like at every possible heat, from rose to bottle green.

encounters.cue: Turn the heat samples over.
encounters.result: The backs carry drawings of bread crusts. An apprentice who could barely read could still judge the firing by supper.

rooms.name: Slip Vat
rooms.description: Fine clay turns the water opaque. A model of a dam seat lies at the bottom under a film of slip.

encounters.cue: Feel the little model under the slip.
encounters.result: A soft strip between the two halves shows where the potter allowed the joint to flex. The strip holds the print of a bootlace.

rooms.name: Glaze Mill
rooms.description: The millstone grinds sea glass until it can be brushed onto pressure gauges.

encounters.cue: Sift the grit at the millstone's lip.
encounters.result: A little blue glass still bears the raised letters of a medicine bottle. Even the gauges were made out of what the district could spare.

rooms.name: Kiln Mouth
rooms.description: The fire is cold. An iron cradle in the ashes is shaped for the return valve at the listening works.

encounters.cue: Inspect the pads of ash inside the cradle.
encounters.result: There are three bare patches where clay feet stood. Raising a piece on three feet let hot air reach its underside.

rooms.name: Coal Eye
rooms.description: A mica window once let a stoker watch the fire without losing their lashes.

encounters.cue: Look closely at the edge of the mica.
encounters.result: Thin leaves peel from the inside. The stoker could strip off a smoke-blackened layer and see the fire again.

rooms.name: Pipe Mould
rooms.description: Two ceramic half-pipes interlock. The bevel on the return half insists that water can run the other way.

encounters.cue: Trace the bevel with a fingertip.
encounters.result: The two halves carry matching dimples. A fitter working blind could line them up by touch.

rooms.name: Drying Strings
rooms.description: Clay whistles hang on strings. The cracked whistles carry a truer warning note than the whole ones.

encounters.cue: Compare the cords on the clay whistles.
encounters.result: Every cracked whistle hangs from a doubled cord. Somebody kept the best alarm whistles from being mistaken for scrap.

rooms.name: Stoker's Bunk
rooms.description: A stoker could judge the heat with one bare foot against the wall. There is a heel-shaped patch of polished brick.

encounters.cue: Examine the polished brick by the bunk.
encounters.result: A cold brick beside the smooth one bears toe marks. The stoker compared them with both feet before waking the next shift.

rooms.name: Saggar Stack
rooms.description: Protective firing boxes are stacked upside down. Their unglazed feet have left rings like tide marks.

encounters.cue: Inspect the rims of the firing boxes.
encounters.result: A scoop in each rim fits a mittened thumb. The oldest scoop has been patched with clay and worn through again.

rooms.name: Ember Court
rooms.description: Nell blows over a red tile and listens to it tick. She builds pressure sleeves and will tell anyone where they go.

encounters.cue: Nell the kiln worker listens to the glaze cooling. She wants one of her sleeves to outlive its maker.
encounters.result: Nell fitted a ceramic sleeve to the listening works return valve. Her maker mark is a bird with one wing. It will hold a split flow if someone sets the trim.

rooms.name: Brick Library
rooms.description: A plan of the district runs along the edges of stacked bricks. Missing bricks have left whole streets blank.

encounters.cue: Read the ends of the map bricks.
encounters.result: Each street continues around the end onto the next brick. A child has pencilled a little ferry across one of the missing rows.

rooms.name: Flue Bend
rooms.description: The chimney turns a right angle here to avoid an older bell cable. The cable is still warm.

encounters.cue: Look where the cable rounds the flue.
encounters.result: A split clay sleeve keeps soot away from the strands. It can be changed without cutting the wire.

rooms.name: Shard Walk
rooms.description: Blue and green shards have been set into the path with their edges down. Boot soles make them sing.

encounters.cue: Tap two neighbouring shards.
encounters.result: The higher note comes from a shard set over a hollow brick. The potters made a door chime wide enough to walk on.

rooms.name: Lime Store
rooms.description: Quicklime is kept on shelves above the highest historic waterline. A new damp patch has reached the bottom shelf.

encounters.cue: Read the labels above the damp shelf.
encounters.result: The old stock marks are in charcoal. At the first splash they smear, warning the mixer which sack to test.

rooms.name: Mason's Bowl
rooms.description: A bowl of soft mortar preserves a message written with the wrong end of a spoon: give the wall somewhere to move.

encounters.cue: Examine the spoon that scored the mortar.
encounters.result: Its handle is cut to the width of a movement joint. The mason could leave instructions and check the work with the same tool.

rooms.name: Annealing Shelf
rooms.description: A warm shelf holds a ceramic egg. If the egg cracks, the big pressure sleeve has cooled too fast.

encounters.cue: Look underneath the test egg.
encounters.result: An unfired twin is sketched on the shelf. Comparing the outlines told the potter how much the clay had shrunk.

rooms.name: Pipe Wagon
rooms.description: A narrow wagon carried finished sleeves to the salt railway. Its brake is tied with ferry rope.

encounters.cue: Follow the ferry rope on the wagon brake.
encounters.result: The loose end is spliced into a loop at knee height. A worker with both hands on a sleeve could set the brake with a foot.

rooms.name: Vent Lantern
rooms.description: Flame flickers sideways through a flue to the listening works. Someone whistles back on the other side.

encounters.cue: Examine the lantern shutter.
encounters.result: A whistle hole pierces the brass lip. The stoker could answer the works through the flue without taking off a respirator.

rooms.name: Cinder Sieve
rooms.description: The last heap has been picked clean of nails. A handful of small brass buttons is all that remains.

encounters.cue: Turn over the salvaged buttons.
encounters.result: Each back has two neat snips through the thread. These buttons were cut from coats before the cloth went for bandages.

links.hint: Draw the lake at the trial weir.
